speaker: attorney
text: Good morning. Would you please state your full name for the record?

speaker: witness
text: Good morning. My name is Rebecca Anne Torres.

speaker: attorney
text: Ms. Torres, where are you currently employed?

speaker: witness
text: I am employed at Meridian Freight, at their downtown distribution facility.

speaker: attorney
text: How long have you worked there?

speaker: witness
text: I have worked there for six years, since March of 2020.

speaker: attorney
text: What is your current position?

speaker: witness
text: I am a shift supervisor on the loading dock.

speaker: attorney
text: As shift supervisor, what are your general responsibilities?

speaker: witness
text: I oversee the loading crew, assign tasks, and make sure safety procedures are followed on the floor.

speaker: attorney
text: Directing your attention to the morning of June the fourteenth, were you working that day?

speaker: witness
text: Yes, I was. I arrived at the facility around six-thirty that morning.

speaker: attorney
text: And where were you positioned when your shift began?

speaker: witness
text: I was near dock door number four, reviewing the morning delivery schedule.

speaker: attorney
text: At some point that morning, did you observe the defendant, Mr. Alan Whitfield, enter the facility?

speaker: witness
text: I did. He came through the east entrance around seven-fifteen.

speaker: attorney
text: What, if anything, did you observe him doing at that time?

speaker: witness
text: He was operating a forklift near bay six, moving pallets toward the storage racks.

speaker: attorney
text: Was that forklift assigned to Mr. Whitfield that morning?

speaker: witness
text: No, it was not. His assigned equipment was a separate pallet jack, not the forklift.

speaker: attorney
text: Did you say anything to him regarding the forklift?

speaker: witness
text: I did. I called out to him and reminded him that the forklift was assigned to another employee.

speaker: attorney
text: How did he respond?

speaker: witness
text: He acknowledged me, but he continued operating the forklift for several more minutes.

speaker: attorney
text: Approximately how many minutes passed before the incident occurred?

speaker: witness
text: I would estimate about ten minutes.

speaker: attorney
text: Please describe, in your own words, what happened next.

speaker: witness
text: Mr. Whitfield was turning the forklift near the end of the rack when the load shifted and several boxes fell from the top shelf.

speaker: attorney
text: Where were you standing at that moment?

speaker: witness
text: I was approximately fifteen feet away, near the scanning station.

speaker: attorney
text: Did the falling boxes strike anyone?

speaker: witness
text: Yes. They struck another employee, Mr. Daniel Reyes, who was walking past the rack at the time.

speaker: attorney
text: What did you do immediately after witnessing this?

speaker: witness
text: I called for medical assistance over the radio and went to check on Mr. Reyes.

speaker: attorney
text: What was Mr. Reyes's condition when you reached him?

speaker: witness
text: He was conscious, but he was holding his shoulder and appeared to be in significant pain.

speaker: attorney
text: Did you speak with Mr. Whitfield after the incident?

speaker: witness
text: I did, once the paramedics had arrived.

speaker: attorney
text: What did he say to you, if anything?

speaker: witness
text: He stated that he had not seen Mr. Reyes walking near the rack.

speaker: attorney
text: Did he say anything about why he was using the forklift instead of his assigned equipment?

speaker: witness
text: He said the pallet jack was slower, and he was trying to catch up on his workload.

speaker: attorney
text: Prior to this incident, had you ever seen Mr. Whitfield operate equipment that was not assigned to him?

speaker: witness
text: Yes, on two prior occasions, though nothing had happened as a result before.

speaker: attorney
text: Did you report those prior occasions to management?

speaker: witness
text: I mentioned it informally to my supervisor, but I did not file a written report.

speaker: attorney
text: Is filing a written report the standard procedure for that kind of observation?

speaker: witness
text: It is supposed to be, yes.

speaker: attorney
text: After this incident, was an incident report completed?

speaker: witness
text: Yes, I completed one later that same day.

speaker: attorney
text: I am going to show you what has been marked as Exhibit Four. Do you recognize this document?

speaker: witness
text: Yes, this is the incident report I filled out.

speaker: attorney
text: Is this an accurate copy of the report you submitted?

speaker: witness
text: Yes, it is.

speaker: attorney
text: Thank you. Let's move to a few follow-up questions.

speaker: attorney
text: Ms. Torres, you testified that you called out to Mr. Whitfield about the forklift. How far away from him were you at that moment?

speaker: witness
text: I was probably twenty feet away.

speaker: attorney
text: Is it possible he did not clearly hear your warning, given the noise level in the facility?

speaker: witness
text: It is possible, though he did acknowledge me with a nod.

speaker: attorney
text: You mentioned two prior occasions where you observed similar conduct. Were either of those occasions reported in writing by anyone else?

speaker: witness
text: Not that I am aware of.

speaker: attorney
text: So there is no written record of those prior occasions?

speaker: witness
text: Correct, not that I know of.

speaker: attorney
text: That's all for cross. Let's go back on the record briefly.

speaker: attorney
text: Briefly, Your Honor. Ms. Torres, regardless of the noise level, did Mr. Whitfield make eye contact with you when you called out to him?

speaker: witness
text: Yes, he did. He looked directly at me and nodded before continuing.

speaker: attorney
text: In your experience as a supervisor, does a nod in that context typically indicate that an instruction was understood?

speaker: witness
text: In my experience, yes, it does.

speaker: attorney
text: Thank you. Nothing further.

speaker: attorney
text: Thank you, Ms. Torres. We're off the record.
